From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — initial technical read

Quick technical read (TL;DR below). I'll follow up with a spreadsheet of capacity math.

Summary TL;DR: Recommend H100-backed Dedicated pool for pilot baseline (memory + perf margin). Consider mixed pool: H100 for latency-sensitive endpoints + a small L4 pool for lower-cost non-critical calls. A100 80GB can work if we secure the 80GB SKU and accept some operational complexity (model sharding or tensor offload).

Rationale and tradeoffs:
- Memory: 13B FP16 with 2k context will push memory for per-request KV cache and activation buffers. H100 80GB gives comfortable headroom for single-replication with no aggressive sharding; A100 80GB is close but often OOM in real-world peaks unless we use tensor-splitting or sequence-length caps. L4 (quantized INT8/INT4) is attractive cost-wise but limited when context/quality/quantization-sensitive prompts are required.
- Latency: For p95 <= 200ms at bursty 80 rps, H100 provides the best chance on single-request fast-paths with smaller micro-batching and pre-warmed KV caches. A100 can match latency if we provision extra replicas to avoid queueing, which increases cost. L4 often increases decode time for high-token responses when model is quantized — good for short responses and embeddings, less so for 400-token avg payloads.
- Throughput & autoscaling: With Redwood continuous batching and KV caching, a single H100 can sustain higher effective rps for short requests; for 400-token averages we should plan 6–10 H100s for steady state with headroom for burst (numbers in attached calcs). If we use A100 80GB, plan +30% replicas to maintain p95 SLO under burst. For L4-only approach we'd need significantly more nodes and risk quality regressions.
- Ops complexity: A100 40GB variants require model sharding (more ops and failure surface). H100 reduces complexity and simplifies fallback behavior. L4 is simplest to spin up but requires a canary of quantized model to validate quality.

Pilot recommendation (concrete):
1) Dedicated pool: start with 8 x H100 (80GB) in US-west for pilot (6 active, 2 warm/burst).
2) Autoscaling policy: scale out by 1 replica per additional 10% CPU/GPU queue for p95 protection, burst-cap of +2 on top of reserved.
3) Fallback: route non-critical requests to a 4-node L4 pool with an INFERENCE_FLAG to mark lower-quality results. Use this for bulk analytics and non-latency-critical processing.
4) Sequence-length policy: enforce dynamic truncation for system prompts and keep history to last 512 tokens to reduce average consumption.

I'll attach the sizing spreadsheet (quantum_sizing_calcs.xlsx) with the latency model and cost delta.

— Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — ops playbook and safety nets

Ops playbook items to include in pilot doc:

1) Warm pools + pre-warming: keep 2 warm H100 instances (no autoscale teardown) to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
2) KV cache sizing: allocate 40% extra mem headroom for KV cache at 2k seq; monitor cache hit rate and increase warm replicas if hit rate < 0.85.
3) Batching knobs: set max micro-batch 4 for H100 to reduce latency tail while preserving token throughput; increase to 8 for A100 clusters when latency budget allows.
4) Graceful fallback: implement model-variant routing allowing seamless fallback from H100->A100->L4 with header metadata marking quality. Keep a small canary traffic fraction on L4 for quality checks.
5) Network considerations: recommend colocating in us-west-2 (low egress to their VPC) and enabling high network priority QoS for inference traffic.
6) Alerts: p95 latency >200ms for 5m -> page SRE + auto-scale immediate + suspend batch window.

I'll add these to the pilot playbook doc and include test scripts to validate p95 at load.

— Hannah
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

1) Pilot baseline: 8 x H100 (80GB) Dedicated nodes in us-west (6 active + 2 warm/burst). This gives the best chance to hit p95 <= 200ms for your 400-token avg workload with 2k context headroom.
2) Cost/term: We propose a 6-week pilot with a 20% pilot discount; Marissa will send a one-page term sheet with ballpark $/hr numbers for H100 vs A100 vs L4.
3) Mixed strategy: keep a 4-node L4 pool for non-critical pipelines and for heavy batch analytics (lower cost). Route lower-quality/non-SLA traffic to the L4 pool.
4) Ops: We'll provision warm pools and the autoscaling policy Hannah suggested; we'll also set up the p95 alerting and nightly KPI reports.

Next steps we need from you:
- Procurement contact + purchase order template
- Confirmation on willingness to accept a limited quantization canary for the L4 pool (so we can validate quality).
- Preferred start week (we can turn up the Dedicated pool within 4 business days after PO).
